evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. I have a new feature request 'Two-factor authentication' to add to TaskFlow. Create it with acceptance criteria, estimate 5 points, label it type/feature + area/auth, and drop it into the current cycle 'Sprint 15'. Show me the exact MCP tool calls and name the reference file of the examples skill that gives the parameter formats. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Concrete calls in order: project(action=list), label(action=list), cycle(action=list, status=current), workitem(action=create) with point and labels, cycle(action=manage_workitems) with add_ids, read back with list_workitems.
expectations: The answer resolves the label names to ids with label(action=list, project_id)
The answer creates the item with workitem(action=create, ..., point=5, labels=[<label uuids>])
The answer finds the cycle with cycle(action=list, project_id, status=current)
The answer adds the item with cycle(action=manage_workitems, project_id, cycle_id, add_ids=[<work item id>])
The answer reads the cycle content back with cycle(action=list_workitems)
The answer names tool-patterns.md as the reference for the exact parameter formats

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Walk me through the full sprint lifecycle from planning to close in Plane. Read the sprint-lifecycle scenario reference and show me the tool calls at each phase. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: The Monday-to-Friday scenario of sprint-lifecycle.md with its concrete calls: capacity, planning, standup, blocker, close and retro.
expectations: The answer puts the sprint capacity at about 15 points
The answer adds the planned items to the sprint with cycle(action=manage_workitems, add_ids=[...])
The answer gets the standup state totals with workitem(action=count, pql='cycle = "<id>"', group_by=state__group)
The answer records the blocker with workitem_relation(action=create, relation_type=blocked_by)
The answer closes the sprint with cycle(action=complete) before cycle(action=archive)
The answer publishes the retro notes with page(action=create)
